subject: Proposal: Dedicated GPU throughput addendum for ApexAI (Q4 traffic profile)
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@apexai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:23:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity: Q4 headroom / throughput addendum request

Hi Vivek —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We reviewed the reserved GPU profile and Q4 traffic patterns with engineering and procurement. Two items came up that we need Redwood to put into a written addendum before corporate procurement will sign the master services agreement:

1) Nightly retrain windows: our models run large nightly retrains (02:00–05:00 local) that produce large token bursts for a short window. We need a temporary queueing carveout so retrain traffic is metered differently from production inference (we're proposing a soft-burst allowance).

2) Throughput floor for peak percentiles: our internal SLIs show the 99th percentile token throughput requirement during Black Friday can be 2.5–3x baseline. Can Redwood guarantee reserved GPU throughput to 95th/99th percentiles or give a documented crediting method when you fall short?

I attached our draft SLA request and a CSV with observed hourly traffic for Oct–Nov (traffic_profile_q4.csv). Procurement wants explicit definitions for (a) what counts as an allowed burst, (b) how credits are calculated and applied, and (c) a mitigation runbook for queueing behavior.

Is Redwood able to produce an addendum (1–2 pages) with concrete numbers we can hand to legal by the end of next week? If feasible we can set a 2-week pilot during first week of December to validate traffic shaping.

Appreciate your help — Elaine
Elaine Park
Head of Procurement, ApexAI
attachments: apex_sla_draft_v2.pdf, traffic_profile_q4.csv
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@apexai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: Q4 headroom / throughput addendum request

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sending the traffic file. We can do an addendum, but to make it operationally safe for both sides we need to align on a few technical knobs and a clear pilot scope. High-level proposal from our side: 

- Temporary "burst carveout" for scheduled retrain windows: provide an opt-in policy allowing retrain jobs to consume dedicated pool headroom with capped burst tokens (configurable, e.g., 3x baseline for up to 3 hours per night).
- Throughput crediting: if reserved throughput falls below agreed percentiles, Redwood issues token credits calculated on a per-hour shortfall basis using a simple formula (shortfall_tokens * 0.5). We'll include an explicit worked example in the addendum.
- Queueing runbook: specify priority lanes (production inference > retrain > batch diagnostics), plus automatic throttles to prevent noisy neighbors.

Before I draft the addendum I need: (1) confirmation of the retrain window timezone (your CSV says PST?) and whether the retrain jobs are pinned to a single region; (2) the 95th/99th percentile numbers you consider mandatory vs aspirational; and (3) whether you want credits applied as monthly invoice-level discounts or as future usage credits.

If you confirm those, I'll produce a 2-page addendum draft for legal review by EOD Tuesday and propose a technical runbook we can pilot. We can also run a quick smoke test during the first pilot night where Redwood routes retrain traffic to an isolated burst lane so both sides can observe latency and token accounting.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0132
attachments: redwood_solution_sketch.pdf

Vivek / Ben —

Quick internal tech notes to feed into the addendum draft: 

- Retrain carveout approach: recommend an isolated burst lane bound to a separate reservation group so retrain KV cache pressure doesn't affect production KV caches. Limit: 3x baseline for up to 3 hours/night, with automatic backoff after 180 minutes.
- Percentile guarantees: we can commit to a 95th percentile reserved throughput at current commit level; 99th percentile guarantees require additional reserved capacity or a capped burst pool (we can offer a quantified burst pool for the pilot).
- Credit calc: suggest credits = min(shortfall_tokens, burst_pool_tokens) * 0.6 for production shortfalls; separate formula for scheduled retrain shortfalls. We'll include example tables (hourly) to make it easy for procurement.
- Observability: require a shared dashboard (read-only) for the pilot period showing per-route token rates and queue depth. Ops will need a 1-hr notice window to enable any temporary manual mitigations.

I'll flag two items for legal: wording for "acceptable scheduled burst" and whether credits are capped monthly. If either is a hard no, procurement should surface it now.

Lauren Bishop
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: Q4 headroom / throughput addendum request

Elaine —

Appreciate the detail. Attached is a concise addendum draft (I pasted the operative bullets below for quick review). If Apex approves these bullets we will: (a) produce the formal addendum for signature, (b) configure the pilot burst lane, and (c) stand up the shared dashboard.

Operative bullets (draft):
- Scheduled Retrain Burst Carveout: Redwood will permit scheduled retrain jobs to access a dedicated burst pool bound to the customer's reserved capacity. Burst pool sizing: up to 300% of baseline throughput for up to 3 hours/night (local time). Retrain windows must be submitted 48 hours in advance for manual enablement in pilot; automated enablement available after pilot.
- Percentile Throughput Commitment: Redwood commits to maintain 95th percentile reserved throughput at the agreed reserved capacity level. 99th percentile performance is supported via the burst pool; failure to meet agreed percentiles will trigger crediting as described below.
- Crediting Methodology: For each UTC hour where observed reserved throughput < agreed threshold, Redwood calculates shortfall_tokens = max(0, threshold_tokens - observed_tokens). Credit issued = shortfall_tokens * 0.6. Credits are applied to the following monthly invoice unless otherwise requested.
- Queueing & Priority Runbook: Production inference is assigned top priority. Retrain and batch jobs are routed to the burst lane. If burst pool exhaustion occurs, Redwood will (1) throttle retrain traffic to baseline rate and (2) notify customer ops and provide a mitigation window.
- Pilot & Validation: Two-week pilot starting on mutually agreed date; Redwood will provide a read-only dashboard and two 1-hour ops calls during pilot nights.

Please confirm whether Apex wants credits as invoice-level discounts or account-level usage credits. Also confirm retrain timezone and whether the pilot can start Dec 6 (we can do Dec 6–19).

If these bullets look good I will send a formal PDF addendum and a DocuSign link to Elaine and Procurement.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 650-555-0189
